articles.title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
articles.summary: Celtic lose to Lask in qualifier from 4-0 up on aggregate. ‘That’s my team and that’s my responsibility,’ O’Neill says. Martin O’Neill has admitted Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager.
body: Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion.

Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20m. O’Neill has overseen more than 300 games as the club’s manager and said it was one of the most painful.
“I would say absolutely, yes,” the 74-year-old said. “I’d put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it’s so, so disappointing.

“We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back.
points: Celtic lose to Lask in qualifier from 4-0 up on aggregate. ‘That’s my team and that’s my responsibility,’ O’Neill says.

articles.summary: Plus: player-managers earning international caps, out-of-position goalkeepers sent off and footballers called up to jury service. Mail us with your all of your questions and answers.
body: “After watching Dom Ballard’s backheel volley for Bristol City against Birmingham in game week two of the Championship, it begs the question: what’s the earliest in a season a goal has gone on to win goal of the season?” asks Ricardio Sentulio.

There is no doubting Dom Ballard’s outrageous flick for Bristol City at Birmingham City should be a Puskás contender, especially with his finish kissing the crossbar on its way in, and has a very good chance of being the best goal scored in the 2026-27 Championship season, even though there is a long way to go.

Ballard’s wondergoal was scored on 22 August, on gameweek two. Eleven years ago to that day, Marco Matias notched this ridiculous effort for Sheffield Wednesday at Leeds United, although it should be said that Yorkshire derby was gameweek four, so technically later in the 2015-16 season than Ballard’s. Matias was given the goal of the season gong in April 2016.

articles.title: Ex-cricketer Will Pucovski takes legal action against former school over concussion
articles.summary: Batter claims 2014 head knock was mismanaged by Brighton Grammar. Pucovski retired from cricket aged 27 after long history of concussions. A private school football coach allegedly directed students to “go in hard” against each other during a training drill a Test cricketer claims left him with the…
body: Former Test cricketer Will Pucovski has launched legal action against his school Brighton Grammar over its handling of a concussion he suffered during an Australian rules football training session in 2014.

Once considered a generational cricketing talent, Pucovski announced his medical retirement from the sport in April last year aged 27. He played one Test for Australia against India at the SCG in 2021 in a career interrupted by head injuries.
In a writ filed in the Supreme Court of Victoria, Pucovski says he experienced at least 13 known concussion injuries from balls to the head throughout his cricket career.
Those exacerbated symptoms from a primary head injury he sustained at the school when he was 16, he claims.

articles.title: Chicago Sky ban Enes Kanter Freedom from home games, calling him ‘a potential threat’
articles.summary: Former NBA center barred from Sky home games. Freedom was ejected after confrontation with Cloud. Owner says Kanter intended to ‘be provocative’ Graham: Kanter is using his freedom to punch down.
body: The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday’s loss to the Indiana Fever.

Owner Michael Alter made the announcement in a rare news conference on Tuesday. Alter told reporters Freedom is not allowed inside of Wintrust Arena for Sky games “unless sometime in the future he’s able to prove to us to our satisfaction that he is able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat”.
The 6ft 10in, 250lb Freedom was removed from Sunday’s game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.
Freedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.”

articles.title: Celtic deficiencies laid bare on another night of Champions League pain
articles.summary: When Callum McGregor eviscerated his own team-mates in the wake of Celtic's stupefying Champions League collapse against LASK, he delivered their one coherent moment of a spineless night, writes Tom English.
body: In branding his fellow players "passive" and "scared" and in then sending a telling shot across their bows - "now we'll see what people are made of" - it is hard to recall him being so full of fury after a European game.
And there are plenty to choose from, plenty of dark nights, plenty of embarrassment, plenty of soul-searching over many years.
For close to a decade he has been Celtic's best player, a near ever-present. That longevity has brought him many trophies, but he's been around for many mortifications, too.

Where losing a 4-0 advantage ranks in the pantheon of Celtic failures is a moot point. What is unarguable is that it was a total capitulation, a feeble collapse in the face of LASK's physicality and desire and belief.

articles.title: What happens when an athlete has a life-changing accident?
articles.summary: Saffron Cresswell was a promising eventer before a fall left her paralysed. Just eight months after first sitting in a canoe, she is heading to the Worlds.
body: Before she had the fall that would leave her paralysed at the age of 23, she had 25 horses that she trained and rode in a business she had been running since she was 15 and was a talented eventer on a pathway towards the Olympics.

Eight years earlier her parents had sold their house to buy a yard to support her career, with the family living in two tiny touring caravans for six years before they converted part of a barn into a home.

For years, Cresswell had been up at 5am, riding four ponies before school, then more afterwards - if she even went in. She puts her school attendance at "68% or something ridiculous" because she was "so busy riding".

'Busy' in fact turns out to be a common theme with Cresswell. During rehab at the hospital, she'd be waiting outside the gym for it to open so she could get an hour in before her physio session was even due to start.

articles.title: Ferrari teases special Michael Schumacher livery for SF-26 at Monza
articles.summary: Ferrari is preparing for the Italian Grand Prix at Monza next week, where there is growing anticipation for the debut of the new engine that should significantly reduce the power gap to Mercedes.
body: As well as the updated engine, the Scuderia has another surprise in store for the tifosi gathered at the 97th edition of the Italian GP: a tribute to Michael Schumacher, the seven-time German world champion who remains in the hearts of all Formula 1 fans.

The Italian round at the Temple of Speed comes 30 years after Schumacher's first win with the red car in 1996 and 20 years after his last victory in 2006. In between, came a decade of success with five world titles and 71 victories, which marked the most glorious period in the history of the Italian team.

The SF-26s of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will therefore have a special livery dedicated to the great champion from Hurth, and the Italian race will be the right stage to acknowledge the role Schumacher earned with extraordinary performances that have since become legendary.

The German is living in an unknown condition following a dramatic skiing accident in Meribel on 29 December 2013. The former champion is lovingly cared for by his wife Corinna and his family, who will have the chance to discover the Formula 1 world's attachment to one of the greatest figures in the history of racing.

Entering the 2026 season, there are a handful of championship-hopeful teams that can continue that trend of dominance along the defensive front.

articles.title: Barcelona face dilemma with new goalkeeper signing after Dinamo Zagreb change loan conditions
articles.summary: Barcelona have completed the signing of Dominik Livakovic, but the Croatian goalkeeper’s future for the coming season remains unresolved as the club’s preferred loan arrangement has hit an unexpected obstacle.
body: The 31-year-old has joined Barcelona from Fenerbahce in a deal worth €2 million plus a possible €500,000 in variables.
After arriving in Barcelona on Tuesday, Livakovic is scheduled to undergo his medical examination on Wednesday before putting pen to paper on a contract running until 2030.
The signing itself is not the issue. The question Barcelona must now answer is where their new goalkeeper will spend the season.

According to SPORT, Barcelona initially planned to send Livakovic out on a one-year loan before integrating him into the first-team setup in 2027, when Wojciech Szczesny 's spell at the club comes to an end.

body: British WBO title holder Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena on Saturday - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

WBA and WBC champion Mayer has no shortage of respect for Cameron - who has won her last four fights since a rematch defeat to Katie Taylor in 2023 - but has backed her own ability to unify the titles in front of what is set to be a hostile Birmingham crowd.
"I feel better than ever," Mayer told Sky Sports. "I just know I just feel unbeatable right now. I feel in a great position and I can't wait to get out to the UK and do my thing.
"[Cameron] is good at what she does. She's an aggressive fighter. She lets her hands go.

articles.title: Wolff 'not at all' disappointed by Verstappen's new Red Bull deal
articles.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says he is "not at all" disappointed by Max Verstappen having committed to Red Bull with a new contract that runs until 2030.
body: Ahead of the Formula 1 season resuming with Verstappen's home Dutch Grand Prix over the weekend, Red Bull ended speculation over the four-time world champion's future by announcing the extension.

While Verstappen's previous deal was set to run until 2028, exit clauses in the agreement meant the 28-year-old would have been free to join another team in 2027, with possible switches to Mercedes and McLaren having been the subject of significant speculation.

However, Wolff has insisted in recent months that he is happy with his driver pairing of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, who sit first and second, respectively, at the top of the Drivers' Championship after Sunday's race in Zandvoort.
Asked about Verstappen's new contract in an interview with Sky Sports F1 on Saturday in Zandvoort, Wolff said: "Most important was that we had the clarity in the team since a long time.

articles.title: Serena and Alcaraz dazzle in mixed doubles before exit
articles.summary: Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
body: Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.
The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."
